title.en: Volume 321 Biographies 108: Qiu Yuexiu, Wu Shaoshi, Yan Xunqi, Wang Jihua, Cao Xiuxian, Zhou Huang, Cao Wenzhi, Du Yulin, Wang Shifen, Jin Jian, Yun Bu
title.raw: 卷321 列傳一百八 裘曰修 吴绍诗 阎循琦 王际华 曹秀先 周煌 曹文埴 杜玉林 王士棻 金简 缊布

sentences.zh: =裘曰修=裘曰修，字叔度，江西新建人。

translations.literal: Qiu Yuexiu. Qiu Yuexiu, style name Shidu, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yuexiu, whose style was Shidu, was from Xinjian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Qianlong and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 自編修五遷至侍郎，歷兵、吏、戶諸部。

translations.literal: From compiler he was promoted five times to vice minister, serving in the ministries of War, Personnel, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from Hanlin compiler through five promotions to vice minister, he served in the ministries of War, Personnel, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 胡中藻以賦詩訕上罪殊死，事未發，曰修漏言於鄉人。

translations.literal: Hu Zhongzao was sentenced to death for composing poetry that mocked the emperor; before the affair broke, Yuexiu leaked word of it to fellow townsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhongzao was condemned to death for poetry deemed to mock the throne; before the case erupted, Yuexiu had let word of it slip to men from his home district.

sentences.zh: 上詰曰修，不敢承，逮所與言者質實，上謂「曰修面欺。」

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated Yuexiu; he dared not confess. When those with whom he had spoken were seized and verified, the emperor said, "Yuexiu deceives me to my face."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Yuexiu, who would not admit it; once the men he had spoken with were arrested and their testimony confirmed, the emperor declared, "Yuexiu lies to my face."

sentences.zh: 二十年五月，下部議奪職，左授右中允。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year the ministry deliberated stripping his office; he was demoted to Right Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year the ministry recommended removal from office, and he was demoted to Right Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 十二月，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth month he had been raised again to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，令在軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was assigned to serve in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 師討準噶爾，命如巴里坤董軍儲。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against the Dzungars, he was ordered to go to Barkol to oversee military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against the Dzungars he was sent to Barkol to supervise army provisions.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「西陲回民數十部落，厄魯特人介其中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized: "On the western frontier there are dozens of Hui Muslim tribes, with Oirats interspersed among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he submitted a memorial: "Along the western frontier stand dozens of Muslim tribal communities, with Oirat peoples scattered among them.

sentences.zh: 當策妄阿喇布坦時恣殺掠，回民久切齒。

translations.literal: When Tsewang Arabtan was in power he killed and plundered at will, and the Muslims had long gnashed their teeth in hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tsewang Arabtan they had suffered unchecked slaughter and plunder, and the Muslims had long harbored bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 請敕伯克額敏和卓，厄魯特竄入境當擒戮，予賞賚，勿被煽生疑懼。」

translations.literal: I request that an edict be sent to the begs and Emin Khoja: when Oirats slip across the border they should be seized and executed, and rewards granted, so that they are not stirred up to suspicion and fear."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the court instruct the begs and Emin Khoja to capture and execute Oirats who crossed the border, reward those who did so, and take care that agitators did not sow mistrust and panic."

sentences.zh: 尋還京師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 河屢決山東、河南、安徽境，積水久不去。

translations.literal: The Yellow River repeatedly burst its banks in Shandong, Henan, and Anhui, and the standing water would not drain away for long periods.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River broke out repeatedly across Shandong, Henan, and Anhui, and floodwater lingered for years without receding.

sentences.zh: 是歲上南巡蒞視，既返蹕，命曰修會山東、河南、安徽諸巡撫周行積水諸州縣，畫疏濬之策。

translations.literal: That year the emperor made a southern tour to inspect in person; after his return he ordered Yuexiu, together with the governors of Shandong, Henan, and Anhui, to tour the flooded prefectures and counties and draft plans for dredging and drainage.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after the emperor's southern inspection tour and return to court, Yuexiu was told to join the governors of Shandong, Henan, and Anhui in surveying flooded districts and drawing up dredging plans.

sentences.zh: 曰修至安徽，偕巡撫高晉疏言：「安徽宿、靈壁、虹三州縣頻年被水，上承河南虞城、夏邑、商丘、永城四縣積水，下注畢匯於宿州。

translations.literal: When Yuexiu reached Anhui, he joined Governor Gao Jin in memorializing: "The three prefectures of Su, Lingbi, and Hong in Anhui have suffered flooding year after year; they receive the accumulated water from the four counties of Yucheng, Xiayi, Shangqiu, and Yongcheng in Henan above, which all pours down and gathers at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Anhui, Yuexiu and Governor Gao Jin reported that Su, Lingbi, and Hong had flooded repeatedly, taking runoff from Yucheng, Xiayi, Shangqiu, and Yongcheng in Henan that ultimately pooled at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 宿州有睢河，虹縣有潼河，泗洲與宿遷、桃源接壤處有安河，皆境內大水，與靈壁、虹縣諸支港當次第疏濬，俾入洪澤湖。

translations.literal: Suzhou has the Sui River, Hong County the Tong River, and at the border of Sizhou with Suqian and Taoyuan there is the An River—all major waters within the province; together with the branch channels of Lingbi and Hong they should be dredged in sequence so as to enter Hongze Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui River runs through Suzhou, the Tong through Hong County, and the An River marks the border with Suqian and Taoyuan—all major interior waterways whose branches in Lingbi and Hong should be cleared in turn to discharge into Hongze Lake.

sentences.zh: 洪澤以清口為出路，上令去草壩使暢流，江南之民，仰頌聖明，宜令每歲應期開放。」

translations.literal: Hongze takes Qingkou as its outlet; Your Majesty has ordered the removal of reed dams to let the flow run free; the people of Jiangnan praise your sagely clarity—it should be ordered that they be opened on schedule every year."
translations.idiomatic: Hongze Lake drains through Qingkou; the emperor had already ordered reed dams removed to ease the flow, to the gratitude of Jiangnan's people, and they asked that the sluices be opened on schedule each year."

sentences.zh: 曰修至河南，偕巡撫胡寶瑔疏陳：「黃河南岸，自滎澤以下諸水，東入睢，東南入淮，皆淺阻不能宣洩。

translations.literal: When Yuexiu reached Henan, he joined Governor Hu Baozhen in memorializing: "South of the Yellow River, from Xingyang downward all the waters that run east into the Sui and southeast into the Huai are shallow and obstructed and cannot discharge freely.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Yuexiu and Governor Hu Baozhen reported that every stream south of the Yellow River from Xingyang eastward—those feeding the Sui and Huai—ran too shallow and choked to carry floodwater off.

sentences.zh: 東境幹河，在商丘為豐樂河，在夏邑為響河，在永城為巴河，實即一水，次則賈魯河，又次則惠濟河、渦河，皆當疏濬。

translations.literal: The main eastern river is called the Fengle River at Shangqiu, the Xiang River at Xiayi, and the Ba River at Yongcheng—it is in fact one watercourse; next come the Jialu River, then the Huiji River and the Wo River—all should be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The principal eastern channel was one stream known as the Fengle at Shangqiu, the Xiang at Xiayi, and the Ba at Yongcheng; the Jialu, Huiji, and Wo rivers ranked next—all needed dredging.

sentences.zh: 自永城至汝寧府支河當施工者凡十二，導積水自支河入於幹河。

translations.literal: From Yongcheng to Runing Prefecture there are twelve branch rivers that should be worked on, to lead accumulated water from the branches into the main river.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve branch channels between Yongcheng and Runing Prefecture should be opened to feed standing water into the main artery.

sentences.zh: 其不能達者，或多作溝渠，或渟為藪澤，潢汙野潦，有所約束而不為民害。」

translations.literal: Where water cannot reach the main channel, either more ditches and canals should be made, or it should be pooled into marshes and lakes, so that wild floodwater is contained and does not harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: Where flow to the trunk river was impossible, they proposed extra ditches or detention marshes to hold field runoff so it would not harm settlements."

sentences.zh: 曰修至山東，偕巡撫鶴年疏請培館陶、臨清濱運河諸州縣民埝，官給夫米，令實力修補。

translations.literal: When Yuexiu reached Shandong, he joined Governor Henian in requesting that the civilian dikes along the Grand Canal at Guantao, Linqing, and other counties be strengthened, with the government supplying rations for laborers so that repairs could be carried out in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong he and Governor Henian asked the state to supply grain for laborers strengthening civilian dikes along the canal at Guantao, Linqing, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 复偕巡撫蔣洲疏言：「山東當疏濬諸水，以兗州為要，曹州次之。

translations.literal: He again joined Governor Jiang Zhou in memorializing: "The waters of Shandong that should be dredged take Yanzhou as the key point and Caozhou as next in importance.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor Jiang Zhou he added that Shandong's dredging priorities were Yanzhou first and Caozhou second.

sentences.zh: 兗州宜治者九水，曹州西南境當濬順堤河，東北境當於八里廟建壩，俾沙河、趙王河水入運，賴以節宣。」

translations.literal: Nine waters in Yanzhou should be treated; in the southwest of Caozhou the Shundi River should be dredged, and in the northeast a dam should be built at Balimiao so that the Sha River and Zhaowang River water may enter the canal and thereby be regulated."
translations.idiomatic: Nine streams around Yanzhou needed work; in southwestern Caozhou the Shundi River should be cleared, and in the northeast a dam at Balimiao should admit the Sha and Zhaowang rivers into the canal for controlled release."

sentences.zh: 曰修諸議皆稱上意，命及時修築。

translations.literal: All of Yuexiu's proposals pleased the emperor, who ordered timely construction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved Yuexiu's plans and ordered work to proceed at once.

sentences.zh: 曰修復至安徽，議濬潁州府境與河南連界者六水，在府境者四水，加疏宿州境睢河，並寬留清口壩口門。

translations.literal: Yuexiu again went to Anhui and proposed dredging six waters along the Yingzhou Prefecture border with Henan and four within the prefecture, with added dredging of the Sui River in Suzhou, and widening the sluice openings at the Qingkou dam.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Anhui, he proposed dredging six border streams and four interior ones in Yingzhou Prefecture, deepening the Sui in Suzhou, and widening the Qingkou dam gates.

sentences.zh: 上獎所議甚合機宜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his proposals as very well suited to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the plan as timely and apt.

sentences.zh: 還河南，諸幹河工竟，議續濬商丘、遂平、上蔡、新蔡諸支流凡五水，並築諸堤堰。

translations.literal: Returning to Henan, when work on the main rivers was finished, he proposed continuing to dredge five branch waters at Shangqiu, Suiping, Shangcai, and Xincai, and building the various dikes and weirs.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Henan, after the trunk channels were done, he urged dredging five tributaries around Shangqiu, Suiping, Shangcai, and Xincai and building supporting dikes and weirs.

sentences.zh: 調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諸水畢治，御製詩褒之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year all the waters were fully regulated, and the emperor composed an imperial poem to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, when the waterways were fully restored, the emperor wrote an imperial poem in his praise.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「諸行省偏災，米豆例免稅。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In provinces suffering partial disaster, grain and beans are customarily exempted from tax.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that in provinces hit by localized disasters, grain and beans were normally tax-exempt.

sentences.zh: 但以免稅故，稽查繁密。

translations.literal: But because of the tax exemption, inspection is extremely strict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the exemption triggered such tight inspection that merchants held back.

sentences.zh: 欲通商而商反以為累，卻顧不前。

translations.literal: merchants who wish to trade instead find it a burden and hesitate to advance.
translations.idiomatic: That merchants meant to bring relief grain found the rules burdensome and held back.

sentences.zh: 請如常收稅。」

translations.literal: I request that tax be collected as usual."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that normal taxes be collected instead."

sentences.zh: 下九卿議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers deliberated and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 京師平糶，曰修言糶價過減，適令商家乘機居積，請石減百錢，數日後市價稍平，以次漸減。

translations.literal: When the capital sold grain at fair price, Yuexiu said the sale price was cut too sharply, which only let merchants hoard opportunistically; he asked that the reduction be one hundred cash per picul, that after a few days market prices would ease somewhat, and then be reduced step by step.
translations.idiomatic: During capital grain sales he warned that prices were cut too steeply, inviting merchants to hoard; he proposed a modest reduction of one hundred cash per picul, then further cuts once the market stabilized.

sentences.zh: 會天津民訟鹽商牛兆泰，兆泰與曰修有連，曰修嘗寄書，上命不必在軍機處行走。

translations.literal: It happened that Tianjin commoners sued the salt merchant Niu Zhaotai; Zhaotai was connected with Yuexiu, and Yuexiu had once sent him a letter, so the emperor ordered that Yuexiu need no longer serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjin residents sued the salt merchant Niu Zhaotai—who was related to Yuexiu and had received a letter from him—the emperor removed Yuexiu from Grand Council duty.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister in charge of the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Granary Department.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，河決楊橋，命如河南勘災賑，並議疏泄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the river broke at Yangqiao; he was ordered to go to Henan to survey the disaster and provide relief, and to deliberate on drainage.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, after a breach at Yangqiao, he was sent to Henan to assess the flood, distribute relief, and plan drainage.

sentences.zh: 曰修請廣設粥廠，饑民便就食；

translations.literal: Yuexiu requested that gruel kitchens be widely set up so that the hungry could conveniently take food;
translations.idiomatic: Yuexiu urged widespread gruel kitchens so the hungry could eat nearby;

sentences.zh: 量增料價，料易集，工可速蕆：上皆可其奏。

translations.literal: and that material prices be raised proportionally so materials would be easy to gather and work could be quickly completed: the emperor approved all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: and higher prices for materials so supplies would come in quickly and work finish sooner—the emperor approved every point.

sentences.zh: 上遣大學士劉統勳、兆惠督塞河。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Grand Secretaries Liu Tongxun and Zhaohui to supervise closing the breach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Grand Secretaries Liu Tongxun and Zhaohui to oversee closing the breach.

sentences.zh: 曰修勘下游，疏言：「黃水悉入賈魯、惠濟二河，二河倘不能容，為患滋大。

translations.literal: Yuexiu surveyed the lower reaches and memorialized: "All the Yellow River water pours into the Jialu and Huiji rivers; if the two rivers cannot contain it, the harm will grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying downstream, Yuexiu warned that if the Jialu and Huiji could not hold the entire Yellow River flow, disaster would spread.

sentences.zh: 宜察堤埝為河水所從入，悉堵禦，俾中流不至复決。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to examine the dikes and embankments by which river water enters and block them all, so that the main current does not break out again."
translations.idiomatic: He urged sealing every dike gap that admitted river water so the main channel would not burst again."

sentences.zh: 曰修還楊橋，疏言河流逼北岸，當挽行中道；

translations.literal: When Yuexiu returned to Yangqiao he memorialized that the current pressed the north bank and should be drawn back to the middle course;
translations.idiomatic: Back at Yangqiao he argued the current hugged the north bank and should be pulled back to mid-channel;

sentences.zh: 又請培補沁水堤，並賑流民：得旨嘉允。

translations.literal: he also asked to strengthen the Qinshui dikes and relieve displaced people: an edict praised and approved.
translations.idiomatic: he also sought repairs on the Qin River dikes and relief for refugees, which the throne approved with praise.

sentences.zh: 曰修子編修麟，卒於京師。

translations.literal: Yuexiu's son, the compiler Lin, died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuexiu's son Lin, a Hanlin compiler, died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上念曰修所領事將竟，有子喪，母老，召還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that the task Yuexiu led was nearly finished, that he had lost a son, and that his mother was old, summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Yuexiu's assignment was nearly done, that he had buried a son, and that his mother was elderly, the emperor recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 工竟，上製中州治河碑，褒曰修及寶瑔不惜工，不愛帑，不勞民，上源下流，以次就治。

translations.literal: When the work was finished the emperor composed the stele "River Control in the Central Provinces," praising Yuexiu and Baozhen for sparing no labor, sparing no treasury funds, and not troubling the people, with upper reaches and lower reaches brought into order in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: When the project ended the emperor erected the "Central Plains River Works" stele, praising Yuexiu and Hu Baozhen for sparing neither labor nor treasury funds nor the people, while bringing upper and lower reaches into order step by step.

sentences.zh: 旋居母喪，歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上以直隸連年被水，曰修服將除，召來京督直隸水利。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, because Zhili had suffered flooding year after year and Yuexiu's mourning period was about to end, he was summoned to the capital to supervise Zhili waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, with Zhili flooded repeatedly and Yuexiu's mourning nearly over, he was recalled to Beijing to direct Zhili's hydraulic works.

sentences.zh: 署吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 河渠工畢，曰修請迎生母就養。

translations.literal: When the canal work was finished, Yuexiu asked to bring his birth mother to live with him for support.
translations.idiomatic: After the canal projects ended he asked permission to bring his mother to live with him.

sentences.zh: 上令會高晉籌濬睢河，曰修言當厚蓄清水以刷淤泥，秋冬水弱，南北築壩堵截，至四月水漲，啟壩分洩，上採其議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to join Gao Jin in planning dredging of the Sui River; Yuexiu said clear water should be stored in depth to scour silt—in autumn and winter when water was weak, dams should be built north and south to block it, and when water rose in the fourth month the dams should be opened to divide and discharge; the emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to work with Gao Jin on the Sui River, he proposed impounding clear water to scour silt—damming the channel in low winter flow and opening the gates when the April rise came—which the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，福建提督黃仕簡疏論總督、巡撫得廈門洋行歲餽，命曰修偕尚書舒赫德往按，並命曰修暫署福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Fujian Provincial Commander Huang Shijian memorialized that the governor-general and governor received annual gifts from the Xiamen foreign trade houses; Yuexiu was ordered to go with Minister Shuhede to investigate, and was also ordered to serve temporarily as Fujian governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, after Provincial Commander Huang Shijian accused the governor-general and governor of taking yearly gifts from Xiamen's foreign merchants, Yuexiu joined Minister Shuhede on an investigation and briefly acted as Fujian governor.

sentences.zh: 讞定，還京師，署倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: When the case was decided he returned to the capital and served concurrently as Vice Minister of the Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: After the case was closed he returned to the capital as acting Vice Minister of the Granary Department.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he received appointment as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，上以江南淮、徐諸河堤前令曰修等經營修築，為時已久；

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the emperor noted that the Huai and Xu river dikes in Jiangnan, which Yuexiu and others had earlier built and repaired, had stood for a long time;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year the emperor observed that the Huai and Xu dikes Yuexiu had built in Jiangnan were aging;

sentences.zh: 復命曰修及高恆往勘山東、河南毗連處，並令巡視。

translations.literal: he again ordered Yuexiu and Gao Heng to go survey the adjoining areas of Shandong and Henan and also to make an inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Yuexiu and Gao Heng to inspect the Shandong–Henan borderlands and tour the works.

sentences.zh: 曰修等疏言：「諸水自二十二年大治後，歲於農隙疏濬，堤岸亦以時培補，現無淤墊殘缺。」

translations.literal: Yuexiu and the others memorialized: "Since the great regulation of the twenty-second year, the waters have been dredged each year in the agricultural slack season, and the dikes have been strengthened and repaired on schedule; at present there is no silting, blockage, or breach."
translations.idiomatic: They reported that since the major works of the twenty-second year, annual off-season dredging and timely dike repairs had left the channels free of silt and breaches."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The report was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The court took note.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，歷禮、工、刑三部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister, serving in the ministries of Rites, Works, and Punishments in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister, serving successively in Rites, Works, and Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，丁生母憂，歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he entered mourning for his birth mother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he went into mourning for his mother and retired home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，召授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was recalled and made Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 初，江南、山東蝗起，命曰修捕治。

translations.literal: Earlier, when locusts arose in Jiangnan and Shandong, Yuexiu had been ordered to capture and control them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had been sent to fight locust outbreaks in Jiangnan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 是歲畿南蝗，復命捕治。

translations.literal: That year locusts appeared south of the capital region, and he was again ordered to capture and control them.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with locusts south of the capital, he was ordered out again.

sentences.zh: 曰修至武清，令順天府尹竇光鼐行求蝗起處。

translations.literal: When Yuexiu reached Wuqing he ordered the Shuntian prefect Dou Guangnai to go and seek out where the locusts were arising.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Wuqing, he told Shuntian Prefect Dou Guangnai to search out the breeding grounds.

sentences.zh: 上責曰修不親勘，左授順天府府尹。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Yuexiu for not surveying in person and demoted him to Shuntian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for not inspecting personally and demoted him to Shuntian prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred back to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，命如滄州勘運河，疏請改低壩基殺水勢，疏下流引河，移捷地閘，裁曲就直，疏減河使順流達海，上從之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was ordered to go to Cangzhou to survey the Grand Canal; he memorialized asking to lower dam foundations to reduce water force, dredge downstream diversion channels, move the Jiedi sluice, cut curves to make straights, and dredge the Jianhe River so the current could flow smoothly to the sea; the emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he surveyed the canal at Cangzhou and proposed lowering dams, dredging downstream diversions, relocating the Jiedi sluice, straightening bends, and clearing the Jianhe so water could run freely to the sea—all approved.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，命南書房行走。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Works and ordered to serve in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Works and was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 命督濬北運河。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise dredging of the Northern Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of dredging the Northern Canal.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，又命督濬永定、北運諸河，疏言：「治河不外疏築，而築不如疏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was again ordered to supervise dredging of the Yongding and Northern Canal rivers; he memorialized: "River control is nothing beyond dredging and building, yet building is inferior to dredging.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he oversaw the Yongding and Northern Canal and argued that dredging beat piling dikes.

sentences.zh: 直省近水居民與水爭地，水退即佔耕，昇科築埝。

translations.literal: Residents near water in the provinces contend with the water for land; when water recedes they immediately occupy and farm it, have it registered for tax, and build embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers along provincial waterways reclaimed floodlands, had them taxed, and threw up embankments as soon as waters fell.

sentences.zh: 有司見不及遠，以為糧地自當防護，逼水為堤埝埝，水乃橫決為災。

translations.literal: Local officials, whose vision does not reach far, think that grain-tax land ought naturally to be protected, press the water with dikes and embankments, and then the water breaks out horizontally and becomes a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Short-sighted officials treated taxed fields as assets to wall off from the river, forcing the current sideways until it burst out in floods.

sentences.zh: 請敕所司，淀泊毋得報墾昇科，橫加堤埝，使水有所歸。」

translations.literal: I request that the responsible offices be instructed that lakes and marshes must not be reported for reclamation and tax registration, and that dikes must not be rashly added, so that water has somewhere to go."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne to forbid reclaiming lakes and marshes for tax rolls or piling new dikes so floodwater could find its course."

sentences.zh: 上降旨嚴禁。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict strictly forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 三十八年四月，曰修病噎乞歸，上以「錢陳群嘗病此，以老許其歸；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-eighth year Yuexiu fell ill with choking and asked to retire; the emperor said, "Qian Chenqun once suffered from this illness and was allowed to retire on account of age;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirty-eighth year Yuexiu fell ill with a choking malady and asked to retire; the emperor replied that Qian Chenqun had been granted leave for the same affliction because of his age,

sentences.zh: 今曰修方六十，不當如陳群之引退。」

translations.literal: but now Yuexiu is only sixty and ought not withdraw as Chenqun did."
translations.idiomatic: but Yuexiu was only sixty and should not withdraw on the same grounds."

sentences.zh: 賜詩慰之，屢遣存問，御醫視疾。

translations.literal: He bestowed a poem to comfort him, repeatedly sent inquiries after his health, and had imperial physicians attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a consoling poem, inquired after him repeatedly, and dispatched imperial physicians.

sentences.zh: 旋加太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the additional title Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous name Wendá.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wendá, "Cultured and Penetrating."

sentences.zh: 子行簡，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xingjian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingjian is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =吳紹詩=吳紹詩，字二南，山東海豐人。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoshi. Wu Shaoshi, style name Ernan, was a native of Haifeng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoshi, whose style was Ernan, was from Haifeng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，世宗命京官主事以上、外官知縣以上，舉品行才猷備任使，即親戚子弟不必引避。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor ordered capital officials of director rank and above and provincial officials of magistrate rank and above to recommend men of character and talent fit for appointment, with no need to avoid recommending relatives.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 the Yongzheng Emperor ordered capital officials from director upward and provincial officials from magistrate upward to recommend men of character and talent fit for office, even close kin.

sentences.zh: 時紹詩世父象寬官湖北黃梅知縣，遂以紹詩應詔，引見，分刑部學習。

translations.literal: At that time Shaoshi's uncle by descent Xiang Kuan was magistrate of Huangmei in Hubei; he therefore presented Shaoshi in response to the edict; after audience Shaoshi was assigned to study in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Xiang Kuan, magistrate of Huangmei in Hubei, nominated him under the edict; after an audience he was posted to the Ministry of Punishments for training.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授七品小京官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given a seventh-rank minor capital post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he received a seventh-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，累遷至郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he rose step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 外擢甘肅鞏昌知府，遷陝西督糧道。

translations.literal: He was promoted outside the capital to prefect of Gongchang in Gansu, then transferred to grain-intendant of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as prefect of Gongchang in Gansu and became Shaanxi grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 總督永常劾紹詩採兵米侵帑，奪職，下巡撫鍾音鞫治。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yongchang impeached Shaoshi for purchasing military grain and embezzling treasury funds; his office was stripped and the case was sent to Governor Zhong Yin for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yongchang accused him of embezzling funds while buying army grain; he was dismissed and handed to Governor Zhong Yin for trial.

sentences.zh: 紹詩以市米貴賤不齊，為中價具報，非侵帑。

translations.literal: Shaoshi argued that market grain prices were uneven and he had reported at the median price, not embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshi replied that uneven market prices had led him to report at a median figure, not to steal public funds.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，發軍台效力，以母病許贖。

translations.literal: When the facts were reported he was sent to serve at a military post, but because his mother was ill he was allowed to redeem his sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The finding sent him to a military post, but his mother's illness won him redemption.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，高宗南巡，紹詩迎蹕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the Gaozong Emperor made a southern tour, Shaoshi met the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he met the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour.

sentences.zh: 起貴州督糧道。

translations.literal: He was restored to grain-intendant of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Guizhou grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 遷雲南按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial judicial commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yunnan judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 調甘肅按察使，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial commissioner of Gansu and then promoted in place to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Gansu as judicial commissioner, he was soon promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 疏言寧夏駐防將軍以下官祿應給粳米，請改徵諸民應納粟米石者，改交粳米七斗，上命寧夏駐防官祿如涼州、莊浪例，改折價。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the salaries of the garrison general of Ningxia and officials below should be paid in polished rice; he asked that where the people owed grain in piculs it be collected as seven-tenths polished rice; the emperor ordered Ningxia garrison salaries to follow the Liangzhou and Zhuanglang precedent and be commuted to cash.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed paying Ningxia garrison salaries in polished rice by collecting seven-tenths of each grain levy in that form; the emperor instead commuted pay to cash as in Liangzhou and Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 又疏鎮番縣柳林湖招墾地，請如安西瓜州屯田例，昇科納賦，較前此徵租歲計有盈，且民戶世業，俾可盡心耕耨，下總督楊應琚等議行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on reclaimed land at Liulin Lake in Zhenfan County, asking that it follow the Anxi and Guazhou military-colony precedent with registration for tax; annual rent would exceed previous collections, and households could make it hereditary livelihood and farm wholeheartedly; the memorial was sent to Governor-General Yang Yingju and others for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged taxing reclaimed land at Liulin Lake under the Anxi–Guazhou colony model, promising higher revenue and stable farming households; Governor-General Yang Yingju and colleagues adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 甘、涼諸縣旱，紹詩复疏言張掖、永昌、鎮番、碾伯、高台五縣舊無城，撫彝廳、隆德、涇州城已損壞，請以時修築，使饑民就工授食，下巡撫常鈞議行。

translations.literal: When Gansu and Liangzhou counties suffered drought, Shaoshi again memorialized that the five counties of Zhangye, Yongchang, Zhenfan, Nianbo, and Gaotai had never had city walls, and that the cities of the Fuyi Pacification Office, Longde, and Jingzhou were already damaged; he asked that they be repaired in season so that hungry people could work for food; the memorial was sent to Governor Chang Jun for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: During drought in Gansu and Liangzhou he asked that wall-less counties be fortified and damaged cities repaired so famine victims could earn food by labor; Governor Chang Jun carried it out.

sentences.zh: 旋以憂歸，三十一年，服除，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned home in mourning; in the thirty-first year, when mourning ended, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home for mourning; when it ended in the thirty-first year he was made Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 出為江西巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以南昌、九江二衛屯田租過重，贛州、袁州、鉛山三衛所租重而田缺，疏請減租，下總督高晉詳勘量減。

translations.literal: Because the military-colony rents of the Nanchang and Jiujiang garrisons were too heavy, and the rents of the Ganzhou, Yuanzhou, and Qianshan garrison posts were heavy while land was scarce, he memorialized asking for rent reduction; the case was sent to Governor-General Gao Jin for detailed survey and measured reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Finding garrison colony rents excessive at Nanchang and Jiujiang and burdensome but land-poor at Ganzhou, Yuanzhou, and Qianshan, he sought reductions; Governor-General Gao Jin surveyed and cut them.

sentences.zh: 上猶產鐵砂，民爭取滋事，疏請募民淘採，募商設廠收鎔，為之條例。

translations.literal: Shangyou produced iron sand; the people fought over it and caused trouble; he memorialized asking to recruit the people to wash and collect it and merchants to set up smelting plants, and drew up regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When fights over iron sand at Shangyou stirred unrest, he proposed licensed folk mining and merchant smelters under new rules.

sentences.zh: 九江關監督舒善、建昌府知府黃肇隆皆以不職為上聞，責紹詩不先事論劾，部議奪職，命寬之。

translations.literal: Jiujiang customs supervisor Shu Shan and Jianchang prefect Huang Zhaolong were both reported to the emperor for malfeasance; Shaoshi was blamed for not impeaching them beforehand; the ministry deliberated stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: After malfeasance by Jiujiang customs chief Shu Shan and Jianchang Prefect Huang Zhaolong reached the throne, Shaoshi was faulted for not impeaching them sooner; although the ministry recommended dismissal, the emperor was lenient.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，召為刑部尚書，未上，調禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was summoned as Minister of Punishments; before he took office he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was summoned as Minister of Punishments but transferred to Minister of Rites before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 是歲南昌等縣被水，十月，紹詩將受代，始奏請緩徵。

translations.literal: That year Nanchang and other counties were flooded; in the tenth month, as Shaoshi was about to be replaced, he only then memorialized asking for deferred collection.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanchang and neighboring counties flooded that year, he waited until the tenth month, on the eve of his replacement, to request tax deferral.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「災地收薄，小民豈能復事輸將？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Where disaster has thinned the harvest, how can the common people again bear the burden of delivery?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "After a thin harvest in a disaster zone, how can commoners pay taxes?

sentences.zh: 紹詩遷延不問，直至開徵將及一月，始以一奏塞責。

translations.literal: Shaoshi delayed and paid no attention until collection was about to open within a month, and only then used one memorial to fob off responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshi ignored the crisis until collection was a month away, then filed a perfunctory memorial.

sentences.zh: 現雖傳諭停緩，急公者納糧不免拮据，疲窘者徒受催科之累。

translations.literal: Although an order has now been sent to halt and defer, those eager to do public duty still strain to pay grain, while the exhausted and impoverished suffer only the harassment of tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Even after orders to defer, conscientious taxpayers were already strained and the destitute had endured needless dunning.

sentences.zh: 此皆紹詩全不知以民事為重有以誤之也。

translations.literal: All this shows that Shaoshi utterly failed to treat the people's affairs as weighty, and that is what led him astray.
translations.idiomatic: All this showed he had never treated people's welfare as paramount.

sentences.zh: 紹詩累經部議降革，並從寬留任。

translations.literal: Shaoshi had repeatedly been subject to ministry deliberation for demotion and dismissal, and each time had been leniently kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had repeatedly recommended demoting him, yet each time the court had been lenient.

sentences.zh: 此則玩視民瘼，難复曲貸。」

translations.literal: This time he treated the people's suffering lightly and could not again be indulged."
translations.idiomatic: This time his indifference to popular distress could no longer be excused."

sentences.zh: 因​​命奪職。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，起刑部郎中，三十六年，擢侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was restored as director in the Ministry of Punishments; in the thirty-sixth year he was promoted to vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he returned as a Punishments director; in the thirty-sixth he became vice minister.

sentences.zh: 皇太后八十萬壽，列香山九老，賜以宴賚。

translations.literal: For the Empress Dowager's eightieth birthday he was listed among the Nine Elders of Xiangshan and granted a banquet and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: For the Empress Dowager's eightieth birthday he was named among the Nine Elders of Xiangshan and honored with a feast and gifts.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，調吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上東巡，迎蹕，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when the emperor made an eastern tour, he met the procession and was given the additional title of minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he met the emperor's eastern tour and received ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，諡恭定。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight and was given the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously titled Gongding, "Respectful and Settled."

sentences.zh: 子垣、壇。

translations.literal: His sons were Yuan and Tan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yuan and Tan.

sentences.zh: 垣，自舉人入貲授兵部郎中，三十五年，特命調刑部。

translations.literal: Yuan, from juren rank, purchased office and was given a directorship in the Ministry of War; in the thirty-fifth year he was specially ordered transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, a juren who had bought office as a War Ministry director, was specially moved to Punishments in the thirty-fifth year.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，紹詩為侍郎，上以垣本特調，命毋迴避。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when Shaoshi was vice minister, because Yuan had been specially transferred the emperor ordered that he need not avoid his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year, with Shaoshi a vice minister, the emperor exempted Yuan from the usual rule against serving under kin because his transfer had been special.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，弟壇為侍郎，乃調吏部。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when his younger brother Tan became vice minister, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, when his brother Tan became vice minister, he was moved to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，以憂歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor and returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he then went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，補原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became a supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以弟壇為巡撫，例不為言官，署吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Tan was governor, by regulation he could not remain a remonstrating official; he served concurrently as director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan became governor, Yuan left the remonstrance posts by rule and acted as a Personnel director.

sentences.zh: 壇卒，復為給事中。

translations.literal: When Tan died he again became supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan's death he returned to the supervising secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五遷為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Five promotions later he was Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，外授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Guangxi in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was posted as governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 五十年，入覲，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he came to court for audience and attended the banquet of a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he attended court and joined the banquet of a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 調湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hubei governor.

sentences.zh: 江夏等州縣旱，疏請緩徵平糶，募商赴四川買米。

translations.literal: When Jiangxia and other prefectures and counties suffered drought, he memorialized asking for deferred collection and fair-price grain sales and to recruit merchants to go to Sichuan to buy rice.
translations.idiomatic: During drought in Jiangxia and neighboring districts he sought tax deferrals, government grain sales, and merchants sent to Sichuan for rice.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，卒，上賜卹，猶獎其實心治災賑也。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he died; the emperor granted condolence gifts and still praised his earnest relief of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-first year; the emperor granted mourning favors and praised his devoted disaster relief.

sentences.zh: 壇，二十六年進士，授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Tan passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year, was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and was promoted again to director.
translations.idiomatic: Tan took his jinshi in the twenty-sixth year, entered Punishments as a clerk, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，紹詩為侍郎，上以壇治事明敏，毋迴避。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, when Shaoshi was vice minister, because Tan handled affairs with clarity and speed the emperor ordered that he need not avoid his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, with Shaoshi a vice minister, the emperor exempted Tan from avoiding kin because he handled affairs with notable efficiency.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，超授江蘇按察使，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted out of turn to Jiangsu judicial commissioner and then promoted in place to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was abruptly made Jiangsu judicial commissioner and soon after provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 江寧、蘇州兩布政所屬，互支官俸兵米，壇疏請更定；

translations.literal: Under the two treasurers of Jiangning and Suzhou, official salaries and military grain were paid interchangeably; Tan memorialized asking for redefinition;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to regularize the tangled cross-payment of salaries and military grain under the Jiangning and Suzhou treasuries;

sentences.zh: 江蘇賦重甲諸行省，每遇奏銷，款目繁複，壇疏請分別總案、專案，以便察覈：皆議行。

translations.literal: Jiangsu's tax burden was the heaviest among the provinces; whenever accounts were submitted for audit the items were extremely complex; Tan memorialized asking to separate general accounts and special cases for easier inspection: all were deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: and to split Jiangsu's heavy, complex tax accounts into general and special ledgers for easier audit—all adopted.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，內擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was promoted within the capital to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was raised to Vice Minister of Punishments in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，太監高雲從以洩道府記載誅，京朝諸臣從問消息者皆奪職，壇亦與。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year the eunuch Gao Yuncong was executed for leaking records of the circuit and prefectural examinations; all capital officials who had inquired after news were stripped of office, and Tan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, after the eunuch Gao Yuncong was executed for leaking examination records, every capital official who had sought tips from him was dismissed, Tan included.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「不意壇竟至於此！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I did not expect Tan to come to this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I never expected this of Tan!

sentences.zh: 念其練習刑名，廢棄可惜。

translations.literal: Considering his mastery of penal law, it would be a pity to cast him aside.
translations.idiomatic: Given his mastery of penal law, it would be a waste to discard him.

sentences.zh: 左授刑部主事。」

translations.literal: He was demoted to clerk in the Ministry of Punishments."
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Punishments clerk."

sentences.zh: 遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to director.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，授江南河庫道，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed intendant of the Jiangnan river granaries and transferred to Jiangsu provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he headed the Jiangnan river-granary circuit and became Jiangsu treasurer.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「吳縣舊有公田萬二千五百畝，銀漕外歲納租息佐轉漕，逋租甚鉅。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Wu County formerly had twelve thousand five hundred mu of public fields; apart from silver tribute grain they paid annual rent interest to assist transport, and arrears were very large.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Wu County's twelve thousand five hundred mu of public fields owed huge rent arrears beyond the grain tribute.

sentences.zh: 以非正賦，遇蠲免不得與。

translations.literal: Because it was not regular tax, when exemptions were granted they could not share in them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rent was not regular tax, the fields missed disaster exemptions.

sentences.zh: 請並予豁除，災歉隨賦蠲緩。」

translations.literal: I ask that all be forgiven and exempted, and that in years of disaster or poor harvest they follow the regular tax in exemption and deferral."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to write off the debt and grant the fields the same relief as regular taxes in bad years."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「江、河險處設救生船五十六，今裁存二十八。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Fifty-six life-saving boats had been set up at dangerous points on the Yangtze and rivers; now only twenty-eight remain.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that only twenty-eight of fifty-six lifeboats once stationed on dangerous reaches of the Yangtze and other rivers remained.

sentences.zh: 請增募四十，分泊京口、瓜州、金山諸處。」

translations.literal: I ask to recruit forty more and station them separately at Jingkou, Guazhou, Jinshan, and other places."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recruit forty more for Jingkou, Guazhou, Jinshan, and other stations."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 紹詩父子明習法律，為高宗所器。

translations.literal: Father and son Shaoshi were well versed in law and were valued by the Gaozong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were expert in law and highly regarded by the Qianlong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 紹詩兩為侍郎，垣、壇在後在郎署，特命毋相避。

translations.literal: Shaoshi twice served as vice minister; Yuan and Tan later served in the secretariats, and were specially ordered not to avoid one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoshi twice served as vice minister; Yuan and Tan later held secretariat posts with special exemption from mutual avoidance.

sentences.zh: 及紹詩移貳吏部，以壇繼其後。

translations.literal: When Shaoshi moved to the second rank in the Ministry of Personnel, Tan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoshi moved to Personnel, Tan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 父子相代，尤異數。

translations.literal: Father and son succeeding one another was an especially rare favor.
translations.idiomatic: A father and son succeeding each other in the same ministry was a rare honor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，重脩大清律例，紹詩充纂修官，綱目二卷，實所釐定。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, when the Great Qing Code was revised, Shaoshi served as compiling editor; the two fascicles of outline were in fact what he determined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, during the revision of the Great Qing Code, Shaoshi served as compiler and drafted the two-fascicle outline.

sentences.zh: 壇复著大清律例通考三十九卷。

translations.literal: Tan also compiled the Comprehensive Study of the Great Qing Code in thirty-nine fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Tan also wrote the Comprehensive Study of the Great Qing Code in thirty-nine fascicles.

sentences.zh: =閻循琦=閻循琦，字景韓，山東昌樂人。

translations.literal: Yan Xunqi. Yan Xunqi, style name Jinghan, was a native of Changle in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xunqi, whose style was Jinghan, was from Changle in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the seventh year of Qianlong and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 散館，授工部主事。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the Academy he was posted to the Ministry of Works as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣東道御史，仍兼工部行走。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became censor of the Guangdong circuit, still serving concurrently in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he became Guangdong circuit censor while still serving in Works.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「江南諸行省水災治賑，應照戶口秤定銀封。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "For flood relief in the Jiangnan provinces, silver packets should be weighed out according to household registers.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Jiangnan flood relief silver should be weighed out per household register.

sentences.zh: 主其事者每假手胥吏，不能無扣減，甚或私用輕戥。

translations.literal: Those in charge always leave matters to clerks, and deductions cannot be avoided; some even use light scales in private.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks handling distribution inevitably skimped, sometimes with rigged scales.

sentences.zh: 宜令督撫派專員監封，仍令道府以時抽驗。

translations.literal: Governors and governors-general should be ordered to assign special officers to supervise sealing, and circuit and prefectural officials should conduct spot checks on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Governors should assign officers to seal packets and circuit officials should spot-check them.

sentences.zh: 貧民以銀易錢買米，當禁奸民剝削。

translations.literal: When the poor exchange silver for cash to buy rice, exploitation by wicked people should be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The poor who exchanged relief silver for cash to buy rice needed protection from gougers.

sentences.zh: 富家積錢，亦應令其散易，以平市價。」

translations.literal: Wealthy families hoarding cash should also be made to release it for exchange to stabilize market prices."
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy hoarders of cash should be pressed to release coin and steady prices."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「循琦所言，頗中情弊。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What Xunqi says hits the abuses fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed that Xunqi had identified real abuses.

sentences.zh: 但若明降諭旨，不肖者未必畏憚；

translations.literal: But if an edict is openly issued, the unworthy may not necessarily fear it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet an open edict might not deter the corrupt;

sentences.zh: 本無此弊者，或轉因此啟其舞弊。

translations.literal: those where the abuse did not exist may instead be prompted to fraud by it.
translations.idiomatic: and places without the problem might learn new tricks from it.

sentences.zh: 當抄循琦奏寄諸行省督撫，令加意體察。」

translations.literal: Xunqi's memorial should be copied and sent to the governors of the provinces, ordering them to pay special attention and investigate."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xunqi's memorial copied to provincial governors for careful scrutiny instead."

sentences.zh: 又疏言八旗義學教習多不實心督課，請歲派大臣會禮部堂官嚴察，上為罷八旗義學，令董理各官學大臣盡心教育。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that instructors in the Eight Banners charity schools often did not earnestly supervise lessons, and asked that each year grand ministers join Rites ministers in strict inspection; the emperor abolished the Eight Banners charity schools and ordered the ministers supervising the various official schools to educate with full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported slack instruction in Banner charity schools and asked for annual inspections; the emperor abolished those schools and ordered the official-school superintendents to teach in earnest.

sentences.zh: 遷轉吏科掌印給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary and seal-holder of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He became seal-holding supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，特命兼吏部文選司郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was specially ordered to serve concurrently as director of the Personnel Ministry's Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was specially assigned to head the Personnel Ministry's Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣侍讀學士，仍兼吏部行走。

translations.literal: He was promoted to reader in the Grand Secretariat and still served concurrently in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Grand Secretariat reader while continuing in Personnel.

sentences.zh: 京西門頭溝煤窯歲久淤塞，有議他處營採者，因緣為利，命循琦會勘。

translations.literal: The coal mines at Mentougou west of the capital had long been silted up; some proposed mining elsewhere and used the occasion for profit; Xunqi was ordered to join in surveying.
translations.idiomatic: When long-silted Mentougou coal pits prompted self-serving proposals to mine elsewhere, Xunqi was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 謂舊窯產煤本旺，鑿溝隧，疏積水，淤去而煤暢；

translations.literal: He said the old mines originally produced coal abundantly; if ditches and tunnels were cut and standing water drained, once silt was removed coal would flow freely;
translations.idiomatic: He reported the old pits were still rich if ditches were cut and water cleared;

sentences.zh: 他處有可採，當以時招商。

translations.literal: where other places could be mined, merchants should be recruited in season.
translations.idiomatic: other workable sites could invite merchants when appropriate.

sentences.zh: 議上，大學士傅恆覆奏如循琦言。

translations.literal: When the proposal was submitted, Grand Secretary Fu Heng memorialized in reply agreeing with Xunqi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fu Heng endorsed his report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，超擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was promoted out of turn to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he was abruptly promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 會試知貢舉，事畢入對，上問：「諸臣知貢舉每有條奏，汝獨無，何也？」

translations.literal: As metropolitan examination supervisor he entered audience when the affair was finished; the emperor asked: "Other supervisors of the examination always submit policy memorials; you alone have none—why?"
translations.idiomatic: After supervising the metropolitan examinations he was summoned; the emperor asked why he alone had filed no policy memorial."

sentences.zh: 循琦對：「科場條例已甚詳備，諸臣實力奉行自足，不敢毛舉一二端自謂曉事也。」

translations.literal: Xunqi replied: "Examination regulations are already very complete; if the gentlemen earnestly carry them out that is sufficient; I dare not pick out one or two points and claim to understand affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Xunqi replied that the examination rules were complete enough if enforced and he would not nitpick to seem clever."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝言是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said he was right.

sentences.zh: 凡事皆當如此，非獨知貢舉而已。」

translations.literal: In all matters one should be thus—not only in supervising the examination."
translations.idiomatic: That should be true of all duties, not examinations alone."

sentences.zh: 三十八年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四十年，卒，贈太子太保，諡恭定。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died; he was posthumously given Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fortieth year and was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with the title Gongding.

sentences.zh: =王際華=王際華，字秋瑞，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Jihua. Wang Jihua, style name Qiurui, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jihua, whose style was Qiurui, was from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he placed third in the first class of jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 he placed third in the top jinshi class and became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十三年，大考翰詹，擢侍讀學士、上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, in the great examination of Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, he was promoted to reader and served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he excelled in the Hanlin evaluation and became a reader in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 廣東舊設兩學政，十五年，以侍讀程岩督廣韶學政，際華督肇高學政，旋用岩議裁併，以憂歸。

translations.literal: Guangdong formerly had two education intendants; in the fifteenth year the reader Cheng Yan supervised the Guang-Shao intendantcy and Jihua the Zhao-Gao intendantcy; soon Cheng Yan's proposal to merge them was adopted, and Jihua returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong once had two education intendants; in the fifteenth year Cheng Yan oversaw Guang-Shao and Jihua Zhao-Gao until Cheng's merger plan was adopted and Jihua went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，起原官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 三遷至侍郎，歷工、刑、兵、戶、吏諸部。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached vice minister, serving in the ministries of Works, Punishments, War, Revenue, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Three promotions brought him to vice minister in Works, Punishments, War, Revenue, and Personnel in turn.

sentences.zh: 在兵部，疏言：「武鄉會試舊例，外場挑雙好、單好、合式三類入內場，雙、單好列東號，合式列西號。

translations.literal: While in the Ministry of War he memorialized: "By the old rule of the military metropolitan examination, the outer field selected three classes for the inner field—double excellence, single excellence, and passing form; double and single excellence were listed in the east section, passing form in the west section.
translations.idiomatic: At War he noted that the military metropolitan exam traditionally sent double-excellent, single-excellent, and merely passing candidates to the inner field, with the first two in the east hall and passers in the west.

sentences.zh: 不肖者見列西號，知不能幸中，紛紛求出。

translations.literal: The unworthy, seeing themselves listed in the west section, knew they could not hope to pass and clamored to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy candidates assigned to the west hall, knowing they could not pass, clamored to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 即有歸號，終日喧嘩。

translations.literal: Even when they had been assigned to their sections, they clamored all day long.
translations.idiomatic: Even after reassignment they kept up the uproar all day.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後武鄉會試，但挑雙、單好，毋更挑合式。」

translations.literal: He requested that hereafter in the military metropolitan examination only double-excellent and single-excellent candidates be selected, and that the passing-form category no longer be selected."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that future military metropolitan exams select only double- and single-excellent candidates and drop the passing-form category."

sentences.zh: 在吏部，疏請在京文武官吏議處，及各部會議外省文武官吏議處，當分別定限，皆如所議。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Personnel he memorialized that deliberation on civil and military officials in the capital and deliberation by the ministries on civil and military officials outside the capital should each have separate time limits—all as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: At Personnel he asked that misconduct cases for capital officials and provincial ones be given separate deadlines, as proposed.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，加太子少傅，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was given Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was made Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，卒，贈太子太保，諡文莊。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he died; he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-first year and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent with the title Wenzhuang, "Cultured and Stately."

sentences.zh: 賜其子朝梧內閣中書，官至山東兗沂曹道。

translations.literal: His son Chaowu was granted a post as Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat; he rose to intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaowu was granted a Grand Secretariat draftership and rose to intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 程岩，字巨山，江西鉛山人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yan, style name Jushan, was a native of Qianshan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan, whose style was Jushan, was from Qianshan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以檢討督廣東肇高學政，移督廣韶學政。

translations.literal: As reviser he supervised the Zhao-Gao education intendantcy in Guangdong, then the Guang-Shao intendantcy.
translations.idiomatic: As a reviser he oversaw the Zhao-Gao education intendantcy in Guangdong, then the Guang-Shao intendantcy.

sentences.zh: 建議裁併，即以命岩。

translations.literal: His proposal to merge the posts was adopted and the assignment was given to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When his merger proposal was adopted, the combined post was given to Yan.

sentences.zh: 官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: =曹秀先=曹秀先，字恆所，江西新建人。

translations.literal: Cao Xiuxian. Cao Xiuxian, style name Hengsuo, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiuxian, whose style was Hengsuo, was from Xinjian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉博學鴻詞，未試，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was nominated for the Erudite Letters examination but did not take it; he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he was nominated for the Erudite Letters exam but did not sit it; he passed the jinshi, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷浙江道御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became censor of the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月，舉恩科會試，秀先從子詠祖坐關節誅，秀先當奪職，上以秀先初不與知，但失察，命寬之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, at the special metropolitan examination, Xiuxian's nephew Yongzu was executed for examination misconduct; Xiuxian should have been dismissed, but the emperor said Xiuxian had not known beforehand and was merely negligent in oversight, and ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, at a special metropolitan exam, Xiuxian's nephew Yongzu was executed for cheating; Xiuxian should have lost his post, but the emperor held that he had not known and had only failed to oversee the matter, and ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 十八年，近畿蝗，秀先請御製文以祭，舉蠟禮；

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year locusts struck the capital region; Xiuxian asked the emperor to compose a sacrificial text and perform the wax-insect rite;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year locusts ravaged the capital region; Xiuxian asked the emperor to compose a sacrificial text and perform the wax-insect rite;

sentences.zh: 州縣募捕蝗，毋藉吏胥。

translations.literal: counties and prefectures should recruit people to catch locusts and not rely on clerks and runners.
translations.idiomatic: and that counties and prefectures should recruit people to catch locusts rather than rely on clerks and runners.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蝗害稼，惟實力捕治，此人事所可盡。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Locusts harm the crops; only vigorous catching and control can help—this is what human effort can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Locusts ruin the harvest; only earnest catching and control can help—that is the limit of what people can do.

sentences.zh: 若欲假文辭以期感格，如韓愈祭噩魚，噩魚遠徙與否，究亦無稽。

translations.literal: If one hopes to move heaven through fine words, as when Han Yu sacrificed to the Crocodile—whether the crocodile moved away cannot in the end be verified.
translations.idiomatic: If one hopes fine words will move heaven, as when Han Yu sacrificed to the crocodile, whether the beast truly departed cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 朕非有泰山北斗之文筆，好名無實，深所弗取。」

translations.literal: I do not have the literary stature of Mount Tai or the Pole Star; empty fame without substance is what I deeply reject."
translations.idiomatic: I do not possess the literary stature of Mount Tai or the Pole Star, and empty fame without substance is what I deeply reject."

sentences.zh: 下部議，罷蠟禮，馀如所請。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the ministries for deliberation; the wax rite was abolished, the rest as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the ministries; the wax rite was abolished, and the rest was granted as requested.

sentences.zh: 七遷至侍郎，歷工、戶、吏諸部。

translations.literal: After seven promotions he reached vice minister, serving in the ministries of Works, Revenue, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Seven promotions brought him to vice minister in Works, Revenue, and Personnel in turn.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，遷禮部尚書、上書房行走，命為總師傅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites and served in the Upper Study, and was appointed chief tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he became Minister of Rites, served in the Upper Study, and was appointed chief tutor.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，禮部議四十七年祀祈穀壇日用次辛。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the Ministry of Rites proposed that the forty-seventh year's Prayer for Grain sacrifice at the Altar of Prayer for Grain use the second xin day.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year Rites proposed that the forty-seventh year's Prayer for Grain sacrifice use the second xin day.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕御極以來，遇正月上辛在初三日前，當隔歲齋戒，改用次辛。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since my accession, when the first xin of the first month falls before the third day, requiring fasting from the previous year, I have used the second xin instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since my accession, when the first xin of the first month falls before the third day and requires fasting from the previous year, I have used the second xin instead.

sentences.zh: 其有初四日上辛亦改次辛者，以為聖母皇太后祝釐，朕率王公大臣拜賀東朝，禮不可闕。

translations.literal: When the first xin fell on the fourth day I also changed to the second xin, because I was observing the Holy Mother Empress Dowager's birthday and leading princes and ministers to congratulate her in the eastern palace—a rite that could not be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the first xin fell on the fourth day I also shifted to the second xin, because I was celebrating the Holy Mother Empress Dowager's birthday and leading princes and ministers to pay court in the eastern palace—a rite that could not be omitted.

sentences.zh: 至明歲正月上辛，則非向年可比矣。

translations.literal: But next year's first xin of the first month is not comparable to previous years.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's first xin of the first month, however, is not comparable to those earlier cases.

sentences.zh: 如謂不敢輕易朝正令典，亦當備稽往例，具奏請旨。

translations.literal: If you feared lightly altering the New Year's audience ceremony, you should have thoroughly searched precedents and memorialized for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: If you feared lightly altering the New Year's audience rite, you should have searched the precedents thoroughly and memorialized for instruction.

sentences.zh: 乃遽行題達，何昧昧至此！」

translations.literal: Yet you hastily issued the proposal—how could you be so dim-witted!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hastily issued the proposal—how could you be so obtuse!"

sentences.zh: 禮部堂官悉下部議，秀先當奪職，復命寬之。

translations.literal: All chief officials of the Ministry of Rites were referred to the ministries for deliberation; Xiuxian should have been dismissed, but again leniency was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: All chief Rites officials were referred to the ministries; Xiuxian should have lost his post, but again the emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，罷上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was removed as chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was removed as chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，卒，贈太子太傅，諡文恪。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he died; he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-ninth year and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent with the title Wenke, "Cultured and Respectful."

sentences.zh: 秀先少孤，事母胡孝，嘗為吮疽。

translations.literal: Xiuxian lost his father young; he served his mother Hu with filial devotion and once sucked pus from her abscess.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuxian was orphaned young; he served his mother Hu with filial devotion and once sucked pus from her abscess.

sentences.zh: 母卒，庶母龔為攜持，事如母。

translations.literal: After his mother died, his concubine-mother Gong raised him; he treated her as his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, his concubine-mother Gong raised him, and he treated her as his own mother.

sentences.zh: 學於兄茂先，事之如嚴師。

translations.literal: He studied under his elder brother Maoxian and treated him as a strict teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his elder brother Maoxian and treated him as a strict teacher.

sentences.zh: 既貴，收宗族，弭鄉里水患。

translations.literal: Once elevated, he gathered his clan and quelled local flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen high, he gathered his clan and quelled local flooding.

sentences.zh: 蒞政勤慎廉儉，罣吏議數四，輒命減免。

translations.literal: In office he was diligent, cautious, honest, and frugal; censured by the ministry four times, each time the emperor ordered mitigation.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was diligent, cautious, honest, and frugal; censured four times by Personnel, each time the emperor ordered mitigation.

sentences.zh: 秀先顏其堂曰「知恩」，紀上眷也。

translations.literal: Xiuxian inscribed his hall "Knowing Grace" to record the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuxian inscribed his hall "Knowing Grace" to record the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 子師曾，自兵部郎中屢遷至侍郎，歷禮、兵二部。

translations.literal: His son Shizeng rose from bureau director in the Ministry of War through repeated promotions to vice minister, serving in the ministries of Rites and War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizeng rose from a War bureau directorship through repeated promotions to vice minister in Rites and War.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年，以兵部失行在印，左授太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, for losing the mobile seal of the Ministry of War, he was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 25, for losing the War Ministry's mobile seal, he was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 道光初，再遷太常寺卿。

translations.literal: Early in the Daoguang reign he was again promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he was again promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 請修墓，歸。

translations.literal: He requested leave to repair his family's tombs and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to repair the family tombs and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =週煌=週煌，字景垣，四川涪州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Huang. Zhou Huang, style name Jingyuan, was a native of Fuzhou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huang, whose style was Jingyuan, was from Fuzhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Qianlong, he became a Hanlin bachelor and, after leaving the academy, was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 2, he became a Hanlin bachelor and, after leaving the academy, was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命偕侍講全魁冊封琉球國王尚穆。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered to accompany reader Quan Kui to invest King Shomu of Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was ordered to accompany reader Quan Kui to invest King Shomu of Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右中允，再遷侍講。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to right assistant reader, then to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to right assistant reader, then to reader.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，使還，奏上琉球國志略，命以武英殿聚珍板印行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, returning from the mission, he submitted Brief Records of Ryukyu; he was ordered to have it printed with the Wuying Hall Treasury Edition blocks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, returning from the mission, he submitted Brief Records of Ryukyu, which the emperor ordered printed from the Wuying Hall Treasury Edition blocks.

sentences.zh: 以從兵在琉球失約束，下吏議，當奪官，上以煌遠使，且在姑米山遇風險，命寬之，仍留任。

translations.literal: Because his escort troops lost discipline in Ryukyu, he was referred to the judiciary and should have been dismissed; the emperor, noting Huang's distant mission and that he had encountered danger at Kume Island, ordered leniency and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his escort lost discipline in Ryukyu, he was referred to the judiciary and should have lost his post; the emperor, noting Huang's distant mission and the danger he met at Kume Island, ordered leniency and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，大考二等，開復。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, with second class in the great examination, restoration was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he placed second class in the great examination and was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左庶子，命上書房行走。
