translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to left vice director of the Supervisorate of Education and ordered to serve in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to left vice director of the Supervisorate of Education and assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated promotions he reached vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十八年五月，命如四川按壁山民訟武生勒派；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirty-eighth year he was ordered to Sichuan to investigate a people's lawsuit in Bishan over a military licentiate's extortion;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirty-eighth year he was sent to Sichuan to investigate a Bishan lawsuit accusing a military licentiate of extortion;

sentences.zh: 十月，復命如四川按蓬溪諸生訟縣吏勒派：俱鞫虛，罪如律。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was again ordered to Sichuan to investigate students' lawsuit in Pengxi against county clerks' extortion: both cases were found groundless and punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was again sent to Sichuan to investigate Pengxi students' suit against county clerks for extortion; both cases proved false and the accusers were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，調兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上幸熱河，煌詣行在入對。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the emperor visited Rehe; Huang went to the mobile court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year the emperor visited Rehe, and Huang went to the mobile court for audience.

sentences.zh: 四川方多盜，號為侂嚕子。

translations.literal: Sichuan then had many bandits known as Tuoluzi.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was then overrun with bandits known as Tuoluzi.

sentences.zh: 總督文綬疏報，遣將吏捕治。

translations.literal: Governor-general Wenshou reported and sent officers to capture and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Wenshou reported the situation and sent officers to capture them.

sentences.zh: 上以諮煌，煌對：「侂嚕子所在多有，縣輒百十人，其渠號'朋頭'。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Huang; Huang replied: "Tuoluzi are found everywhere, often a hundred or more in a county; their leaders are called 'band heads.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Huang, who replied, "Tuoluzi are found everywhere, often a hundred or more in a county; their leaders are called 'band heads.

sentences.zh: 白日劫掠，將吏置不問。

translations.literal: They plunder by daylight and officers ignore them.
translations.idiomatic: They plunder in broad daylight while officers look the other way.

sentences.zh: 甚且州縣胥役亦為之，大竹縣役子為盜渠，號一隻虎。」

translations.literal: Even county clerks and runners join them; a runner's son in Dazhu became a band chief called One-Eyed Tiger."
translations.idiomatic: Even county clerks and runners join them; a runner's son in Dazhu became a band chief called One-Eyed Tiger."

sentences.zh: 上為罷文綬，調福康安督四川，命防護煌所居村。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Wenshou, transferred Fuk'anggan to govern Sichuan, and ordered protection for the village where Huang lived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Wenshou, transferred Fuk'anggan to govern Sichuan, and ordered protection for Huang's home village.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，命為上書房總師傅，未逾年，以煌不勝總師傅，罷之。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study; within a year, because Huang was unsuited to chief tutor, he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study, but within a year, finding Huang unsuited to the post, the emperor removed him.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，調左都御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was transferred to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he was transferred to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五十年，以病乞休，詔以兵部尚書加太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, ill, he requested retirement; an edict granted retirement as Minister of War with Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he pleaded illness and asked to retire; an edict granted him retirement as Minister of War with the rank of Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，進太子太傅，賜祭葬，諡文恭。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, granted sacrificial honors at burial, and given the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, granted sacrificial honors at burial, and given the title Wengong, "Cultured and Reverent."

sentences.zh: 子興岱，字冠三。

translations.literal: His son Xingdai, style name Guansan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingdai, whose style was Guansan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, he became a Hanlin bachelor and, after leaving the academy, was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 36, he became a Hanlin bachelor and, after leaving the academy, was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated promotions he reached expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 超授內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was extraordinarily appointed grand secretary assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was extraordinarily appointed grand secretary assistant.

sentences.zh: 擢侍郎，歷禮、吏、戶諸部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister, serving in the ministries of Rites, Personnel, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister in Rites, Personnel, and Revenue in turn.

sentences.zh: 命在南書房行走。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，祭告川、陝岳瀆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he performed sacrificial announcements at the mountains and rivers of Sichuan and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he performed sacrificial announcements at the mountains and rivers of Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 川、楚教匪亂方急，上命興岱經被寇州縣宣諭慰卹，並傳詔招撫；

translations.literal: With the Sichuan-Hubei White Lotus rebellion urgent, the emperor ordered Xingdai to tour stricken counties proclaiming comfort and relief and to convey edicts offering amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: With the Sichuan-Hubei White Lotus rebellion urgent, the emperor ordered Xingdai to tour stricken counties proclaiming comfort and relief and to convey edicts offering amnesty;

sentences.zh: 復以軍中諸將勇怯諮興岱。

translations.literal: The emperor also consulted Xingdai on the courage and cowardice of the generals in the field.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also consulted Xingdai on the courage and cowardice of the generals in the field.

sentences.zh: 興岱奏：「臣行次廣元，民言總兵硃射斗在高院場戰敗，總督魁倫未遣兵應援，又不​​嚴守潼關。

translations.literal: Xingdai memorialized: "Passing through Guangyuan, the people said General Zhu Shedou was defeated at Gaoyuanchang, Governor-general Kuilun sent no reinforcements, and did not strictly hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Xingdai memorialized, "Passing through Guangyuan, the people said General Zhu Shedou had been defeated at Gaoyuanchang, that Governor-general Kuilun sent no reinforcements, and that he did not strictly hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊夜掠太和鎮，焚殺甚酷。

translations.literal: Bandits raided Taihe town by night with cruel burning and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits raided Taihe town by night with cruel burning and killing.

sentences.zh: 行次梓潼，賊正擾縣境，民紛紛徙避。

translations.literal: At Zitong bandits were harassing the county and the people fled in droves.
translations.idiomatic: At Zitong bandits were harassing the county, and the people fled in droves.

sentences.zh: 臣在縣督率嚴防，駐二日乃行，途中宣上指慰諭。

translations.literal: I supervised defenses there for two days before moving on, proclaiming the emperor's instructions along the way.
translations.idiomatic: I supervised defenses there for two days before moving on, proclaiming the emperor's instructions along the way.

sentences.zh: 民言川軍逐賊，德楞泰最奮勇，且能於臨陣廣布德意，解散脅從。

translations.literal: The people said that among Sichuan troops pursuing bandits, Delingtai was most brave and could spread benevolent intent in battle, disbanding coerced followers.
translations.idiomatic: The people said that among Sichuan troops pursuing bandits, Delingtai was the most daring and could spread benevolent intent in battle, disbanding coerced followers.

sentences.zh: 但賊勢方張，一人不能兼顧。

translations.literal: But bandit power was surging; one man could not cover everything.
translations.idiomatic: But bandit power was surging, and one man could not cover everything.

sentences.zh: 請敕督兵諸大臣同心協力。」

translations.literal: I ask that the emperor instruct the supervising ministers and commanders to work in concert."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the emperor instruct the supervising ministers and commanders to work in concert."

sentences.zh: 上奪魁倫官，逮詣成都，命興岱會勒保按鞫。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Kuilun of office, had him brought to Chengdu, and ordered Xingdai to join Lebao in investigating.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Kuilun of office, had him brought to Chengdu, and ordered Xingdai to join Lebao in investigating the case.

sentences.zh: 事畢，還京師。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was finished, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 煌嘗兩使四川按事，興岱复繼之，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Huang had twice been sent to Sichuan on investigations; Xingdai followed in his footsteps, and at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had twice been sent to Sichuan on investigations, and Xingdai followed in his footsteps—a source of pride at the time.

sentences.zh: 六年，充江西考官，坐受餽，並索取衣裘，命退出南書房，左授侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, serving as Jiangxi examiner, he was convicted of accepting gifts and demanding furs; he was ordered out of the Southern Study and demoted to reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, while serving as Jiangxi examiner, he was convicted of accepting gifts and demanding furs; he was ordered out of the Southern Study and demoted to reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 八年，大考，以老乞休，上從之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, at the great examination, he pleaded old age for retirement; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, at the great examination, he pleaded old age and asked to retire; the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 旋复授編修，遷侍講。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed compiler and promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed compiler and promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士，复再遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand secretary assistant, then again to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand secretary assistant, then again to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: =曹文埴=曹文埴，字竹虛，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi. Cao Wenzhi, style name Zhuxu, was a native of She county in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi, whose style was Zhuxu, was from She county in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年二甲一名進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Top of the second class of jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, he became a Hanlin bachelor and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Top of the second jinshi class in Qianlong 25, he became a Hanlin bachelor and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 直懋勤殿，四遷翰林院侍讀學士，命在南書房行走。

translations.literal: He served in the Hall of Reverence and Diligence; after four promotions he became reader of the Hanlin Academy and was ordered to the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Hall of Reverence and Diligence, rose through four promotions to reader of the Hanlin Academy, and was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 再遷詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to grand tutor of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to grand tutor of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，歸。

translations.literal: In mourning for his father, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，詣京師，謁孝聖憲皇后梓宮。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he came to the capital to attend the coffin of Empress Xiaoshengxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he came to the capital to attend the coffin of Empress Xiaoshengxian.

sentences.zh: 喪終，仍在南書房行走。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he again served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he again served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 授左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎，歷刑、兵、工、戶諸部，兼管順天府府尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister, serving in the ministries of Punishments, War, Works, and Revenue, and also overseeing the Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister in Punishments, War, Works, and Revenue in turn, and also oversaw the Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 軍機章京、員外郎海昇毆殺其妻，以自縊報，其妻弟貴寧爭非是。

translations.literal: Grand Council clerk and vice director Hai Sheng beat his wife to death and reported it as self-strangulation; his wife's younger brother Guining disputed that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council clerk and vice director Hai Sheng murdered his wife but reported that she had hanged herself; her younger brother Guining insisted the account was false.

sentences.zh: 命左都御史紀昀等驗屍，仍以自縊具獄。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Left Censor-in-Chief Ji Yun and others to examine the corpse; they still closed the case as self-strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Censor-in-Chief Ji Yun and others to examine the body, but they still concluded the case as suicide by hanging.

sentences.zh: 貴寧复爭言：「海昇與大學士阿桂有連，驗不實。」

translations.literal: Guining again disputed, saying: "Hai Sheng has ties to Grand Secretary Agui; the examination was not truthful."
translations.idiomatic: Guining protested again: "Hai Sheng is connected to Grand Secretary Agui, and the autopsy was not honest."

sentences.zh: 更命文埴與侍郎伊齡阿覆驗，得毆殺狀，以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Cao Wenzhi and Vice Minister Yiling'a to re-examine the body; they found evidence of beating to death and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Cao Wenzhi and Vice Minister Yiling'a to re-examine the corpse; they found signs of beating and reported the truth.

sentences.zh: 上獎文埴等不徇隱，公正得大臣體。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Cao Wenzhi and the others for not showing partiality; their fairness befitted great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Cao Wenzhi and his colleagues for refusing to conceal the facts, saying their impartiality befitted true ministers of state.

sentences.zh: 阿桂以嘗奏及語袒海昇，坐罰俸，昀下吏議，刑部侍郎景祿、杜玉林及郎中王士棻等皆遣戍。

translations.literal: Agui was fined a year's salary for having previously memorialized and spoken in Hai Sheng's favor; Ji Yun was handed over to officials for deliberation; Vice Minister of Punishments Jing Lu, Du Yulin, and Director Wang Shifen and others were all sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was fined a year's salary for having earlier memorialized and spoken on Hai Sheng's behalf; Ji Yun was handed over for official deliberation; Vice Minister Jing Lu of Punishments, Du Yulin, Director Wang Shifen, and others were all banished.

sentences.zh: 擢文埴戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 復命與伊齡阿如通州督漕政，漕船回空較早，命議敘。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to go with Yiling'a to Tongzhou to oversee grain transport; the grain boats returned empty earlier than usual, and the emperor ordered deliberation on rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent with Yiling'a to Tongzhou to supervise the grain transport system; because the grain boats returned empty earlier than usual, the emperor ordered a review for merit awards.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，命如浙江察倉庫虧缺。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was ordered to Zhejiang to investigate deficits in the granaries and storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was dispatched to Zhejiang to investigate shortages in the granaries and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 旋復命阿桂會文埴董理。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Agui was ordered to join Cao Wenzhi in supervising the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Agui was ordered to join Cao Wenzhi in directing the investigation.

sentences.zh: 浙江濱海建石塘，外積柴為障，是為柴塘。

translations.literal: Along the Zhejiang coast stone dikes were built; outside them brushwood was piled as a barrier—this was called the brushwood dike.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Zhejiang coast stone seawalls were built, with brushwood piled outside as a barrier—what was known as the chaitang, or brushwood dike.

sentences.zh: 外又累土為坡以護，是​​為坦水。

translations.literal: Outside that, earth was piled into slopes for protection—this was called the tan water slope.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, earth was heaped into protective slopes—what was called the tan water apron.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福崧疏請籌歲修，命文埴並按。

translations.literal: Governor Fu Song memorialized requesting funds for annual repairs; Cao Wenzhi was ordered to investigate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Song memorialized asking that funds be set aside for annual repairs, and Cao Wenzhi was ordered to investigate the matter jointly.

sentences.zh: 文埴言：「柴塘日受潮汐，往來汕刷，勢不能無蹲蕣。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi said: "The brushwood dike daily suffers the tides; with constant washing back and forth, it cannot avoid subsidence and decay.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi wrote: "The brushwood dike is daily battered by the tides; with the constant scouring of the water, it will inevitably sink and crumble in places.

sentences.zh: 今既為坦水，若不以時補修，不足當潮勢而為石塘之保障。」

translations.literal: Now that it serves as tan water, if it is not repaired in season, it will not suffice to meet the force of the tide and protect the stone dike."
translations.idiomatic: Now that it serves as the tan water apron, if it is not repaired on schedule it will not hold back the tide or shield the stone seawall."

sentences.zh: 得旨，如所議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, adopting his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 文埴還京師。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以阿桂及文埴鞫平陽知縣黃梅未得實，下部議，降二級，命寬之。

translations.literal: Because Agui and Cao Wenzhi had tried Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, without establishing the facts, the emperor referred the matter to the ministry for deliberation; they were to be demoted two ranks, but the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Because Agui and Cao Wenzhi had tried Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, without establishing the facts, the case went to the ministry for deliberation and they were to be demoted two ranks, though the emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，文埴以母老乞歸養，俞其請，加太子太保，御書賜其母。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Cao Wenzhi requested leave to return home to care for his aged mother; his request was granted, he was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and the emperor's own calligraphy was bestowed on his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year Cao Wenzhi asked to return home to care for his elderly mother; the request was granted, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and the emperor's own calligraphy was bestowed on his mother.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，上以明年八十萬壽，命文埴毋詣京師。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, with the emperor's eightieth birthday the following year, Cao Wenzhi was told not to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year, with the emperor's eightieth birthday approaching the next year, Cao Wenzhi was told not to travel to the capital.

sentences.zh: 文埴疏言：「母健在，明年當詣京師祝嘏。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi memorialized: "My mother is still living; next year I ought to come to the capital to offer birthday congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi memorialized: "My mother is still alive, and next year I should come to the capital to offer birthday congratulations.

sentences.zh: 至時如未能遠離，當自審度。

translations.literal: When the time comes, if I cannot leave her side, I shall judge for myself.
translations.idiomatic: When the time comes, if I cannot leave her, I shall decide for myself.

sentences.zh: 上體聖意，下順親心，諸事皆從實。」

translations.literal: I honor Your Majesty's intent above and my mother's wishes below; in all things I speak truly."
translations.idiomatic: I would honor Your Majesty's wishes above and my mother's heart below, and in all things speak honestly."

sentences.zh: 得旨：「卿能來，朕誠喜，但毋稍勉強。」

translations.literal: The reply came: "If you can come, I shall indeed be glad—but do not force yourself at all."
translations.idiomatic: The reply read: "If you can come, I shall truly be glad—but do not strain yourself in the least."

sentences.zh: 五十五年，文埴詣京師祝嘏，上賜​​文埴母大緞、貂皮。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year Cao Wenzhi came to the capital to offer birthday congratulations; the emperor bestowed heavy silk damask and sable fur on Cao Wenzhi's mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year Cao Wenzhi came to the capital to offer birthday congratulations, and the emperor bestowed heavy silk damask and sable fur on his mother.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，禦試翰詹，文埴子編修振鏞列三等。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, at the palace examination for Hanlin and Hanlin attendants, Cao Wenzhi's son, compiler Zhenyong, was placed in the third class.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year, at the palace examination for Hanlin scholars, Cao Wenzhi's son, compiler Zhenyong, ranked in the third class.

sentences.zh: 上以才可造，又為文埴子，擢侍講。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed his talent promising and, as Cao Wenzhi's son, promoted him to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged his talent worth cultivating and, as Cao Wenzhi's son, promoted him to expositor.

sentences.zh: 寄賜文埴御製文勒石拓本。

translations.literal: By post the emperor bestowed on Cao Wenzhi a rubbing of imperial composition engraved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: By courier the emperor sent Cao Wenzhi a rubbing of an imperial text engraved on stone.

sentences.zh: 六十年，以上御極週甲子，文埴詣京師賀，上复賜文埴母御書、文綺、貂皮。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, on the sixtieth anniversary of the emperor's accession, Cao Wenzhi came to the capital to offer congratulations; the emperor again bestowed imperial calligraphy, patterned silk, and sable fur on Cao Wenzhi's mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, on the sixtieth anniversary of the emperor's accession, Cao Wenzhi came to the capital to offer congratulations, and the emperor again bestowed imperial calligraphy, patterned silk, and sable fur on his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 高宗方有疾，卹典未行。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong was then ill, and the condolence rites were not yet performed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was then ill, and the state mourning rites had not yet been granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，仁宗命予卹，諡文敏，並賜文埴母大緞、人參。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Renzong ordered condolence rites granted; the posthumous title Wenmin was given, and heavy silk damask and ginseng were bestowed on Cao Wenzhi's mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Emperor Renzong ordered mourning honors granted; he was given the posthumous title Wenmin, and heavy silk damask and ginseng were bestowed on Cao Wenzhi's mother.

sentences.zh: 乾隆之季，和珅專政，嫉阿桂功高位其上。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianlong reign Heshen held sole power and resented Agui for his achievements and rank above him.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Qianlong reign Heshen monopolized power and resented Agui for his achievements and for standing above him in rank.

sentences.zh: 海昇妻之獄，辭連阿桂。

translations.literal: In the case of Hai Sheng's wife, testimony implicated Agui.
translations.idiomatic: In the case of Hai Sheng's wife, the testimony implicated Agui.

sentences.zh: 和申妄謂文埴能立異同，欲引以為重。

translations.literal: Heshen vainly supposed Cao Wenzhi could stand apart with a dissenting view and wished to bring him in to add weight.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen wrongly assumed Cao Wenzhi would break ranks and offer a dissenting view, and hoped to enlist him to lend weight to his side.

sentences.zh: 文埴特持正，故非阿和珅，母老決引退，恩禮弗替。

translations.literal: Cao Wenzhi held especially to rectitude and therefore did not defer to Heshen; when his mother aged he firmly withdrew, yet imperial favor and ceremony never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi held firmly to what was right and would not defer to Heshen; when his mother grew old he resolutely retired, yet imperial favor never waned.

sentences.zh: 子振鏞，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zhenyong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenyong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: =杜玉林=杜玉林，字凝台，江蘇金匱人。

translations.literal: Du Yulin. Du Yulin, style name Ningtai, was a native of Jingui in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yulin, whose style was Ningtai, was from Jingui in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年進士，授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the nineteenth year of Qianlong; appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Punishments; after two promotions, director.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Qianlong 19, entered the Ministry of Punishments as a chief clerk, and after two promotions became a director.

sentences.zh: 外授江西南康知府，三遷四川布政使。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Nankang in Jiangxi; after three promotions, fiscal commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Nankang in Jiangxi, and after three promotions became fiscal commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，內擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was promoted from within to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he was raised from within the capital to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，命如四川按會理州沙金鳳訴其兄土司金龍佔田獄。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was ordered to Sichuan to investigate the case in Huili wherein Sha Jinfeng sued his elder brother, native chieftain Jin Long, for seizing his fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was sent to Sichuan to investigate the case in Huili in which Sha Jinfeng sued his elder brother, native chieftain Jin Long, for seizing his land.

sentences.zh: 讞定，金鳳复詣京師呈訴，覆讞如玉林議分田，惟獄情未盡，又知州徐士勳當劾，玉林以同鄉置不問。

translations.literal: After the judgment was fixed, Jinfeng again came to the capital to petition; on re-judgment the fields were divided as Yulin had proposed, but the facts of the case were not fully exhausted, and Prefect Xu Shixun ought to have been impeached; Yulin, being a fellow townsman, let the matter pass without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: After the verdict was settled, Jinfeng again petitioned in the capital; on review the land was divided as Yulin had proposed, but the facts were not fully pursued, and Prefect Xu Shixun should have been impeached—yet Yulin, as a fellow townsman, let it pass.

sentences.zh: 吏議當左遷，上授玉林工部侍郎，仍領刑部事。

translations.literal: Official deliberation called for demotion; the emperor appointed Yulin vice minister of Works while he still held charge of Punishments affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Official deliberation called for demotion, but the emperor appointed Yulin vice minister of Works while he continued to handle Punishments affairs.

sentences.zh: 旋復還刑部，迭使湖南北、江南讞獄。

translations.literal: Shortly he returned to Punishments and was repeatedly sent to Hunan, Hubei, and Jiangnan to judge cases.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Punishments and was repeatedly sent to Hunan, Hubei, and Jiangnan to adjudicate cases.

sentences.zh: 尚書福隆安僕笞殺役夫，賄他人自代，玉林不能察，降三品冠服。

translations.literal: Minister Fu Long'an's servant beat a laborer to death; he bribed another to take his place, and Yulin failed to detect it; he was reduced to third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Fu Long'an's servant beat a laborer to death and bribed another man to take the blame; Yulin failed to uncover the substitution and was reduced to third-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 旋命復本秩。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered restored to his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered restored to his original rank.

sentences.zh: 五十年，坐海昇妻獄，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, implicated in the case of Hai Sheng's wife, he was exiled to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, implicated in the case of Hai Sheng's wife, he was banished to Yili.

sentences.zh: 明年，召還。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 授刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 行至涇州，卒。

translations.literal: En route at Jingzhou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 玉林善治獄，嘗曰：「刑一成而不變。

translations.literal: Yulin was skilled at hearing cases and once said: "Once punishment is fixed it should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin was skilled at judging cases and once said: "Punishment, once fixed, should not be altered.

sentences.zh: 治律例猶善醫，貴不泥於方書，而察其受病之實。

translations.literal: Handling statutes and precedents is like practicing medicine well: what matters is not clinging to prescription books but discerning the actual affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Handling statutes and precedents is like practicing medicine well: one must not cling blindly to formulary texts but discern the actual disease.

sentences.zh: 不如是無以臨民。」

translations.literal: Without this one cannot rightly govern the people."
translations.idiomatic: Without that one cannot rightly judge for the people."

sentences.zh: =王士棻=王士棻，字蘭圃，陝西華州人。

translations.literal: Wang Shifen. Wang Shifen, style name Lanpu, was a native of Huazhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifen, whose style was Lanpu, was from Huazhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年進士，改庶吉士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the nineteenth year of Qianlong; became Hanlin bachelor; appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Qianlong 19, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: After two promotions, director.
translations.idiomatic: After two promotions he became a director.

sentences.zh: 和珅為步軍統領，寵其役，役佔通州車行。

translations.literal: Heshen was commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade; he favored his bond servants, and a servant seized a carting business in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen was commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Brigade; he favored his bond servants, and one of them seized a carting business in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 州民訴刑部，士棻為定讞，戍其役黑龍江。

translations.literal: Townsmen of the prefecture sued before the Ministry of Punishments; Shifen fixed the judgment and sent the servant into exile in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople sued before the Ministry of Punishments; Shifen rendered the verdict and banished the servant to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 上詣碧雲寺禮佛，訝池涸，問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Biyun Temple to worship the Buddha, was surprised to find the pond dry, and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Biyun Temple to worship the Buddha, was astonished to find the pond dry, and asked why.

sentences.zh: 僧言寺後開煤礦，引水別流。

translations.literal: A monk said a coal mine had been opened behind the temple and the water had been diverted elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: A monk said a coal mine had been opened behind the temple and its water diverted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上怒，逮主其事者下刑部，則和珅奴也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, had those responsible seized and sent to the Ministry of Punishments—it turned out to be Heshen's slave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had those responsible seized and sent to the Ministry of Punishments—and they proved to be Heshen's slaves.

sentences.zh: 諸曹憚和珅，不欲竟其獄，士棻復為定讞。

translations.literal: The various bureaus feared Heshen and did not wish to bring the case to completion; Shifen again fixed the judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus feared Heshen and were unwilling to see the case through; Shifen again rendered the verdict.

sentences.zh: 上責和珅而誅其奴。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Heshen and had his slave executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Heshen and had the slave executed.

sentences.zh: 五十年四月，海昇妻之獄，刑部侍郎杜玉林坐驗屍不以實，當譴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fiftieth year, in the case of Hai Sheng's wife, Vice Minister Du Yulin was liable for not examining the corpse truthfully and due for censure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fiftieth year, in the case of Hai Sheng's wife, Vice Minister Du Yulin was found to have autopsied the body dishonestly and was due for punishment.

sentences.zh: 上欲以士棻代，而士棻亦佐驗。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to replace him with Shifen, but Shifen had also assisted in the examination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to replace him with Shifen, but Shifen had also assisted in the autopsy.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「王士棻在刑部年久，前因召對，觀其人尚有才，方欲量加擢用。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Wang Shifen has been in the Ministry of Punishments many years; when summoned earlier I observed he still had talent and was about to promote him accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wang Shifen has served in the Ministry of Punishments for many years; when I summoned him earlier I saw he still had ability and was about to promote him.

sentences.zh: 乃覆驗回護，逢迎阿桂，罪無可逭。」

translations.literal: Yet on re-examination he shielded the guilty and curried favor with Agui—his guilt admits no excuse."
translations.idiomatic: Yet on re-examination he shielded the guilty and ingratiated himself with Agui—his offense brooks no excuse."

sentences.zh: 遂與玉林戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Yulin were exiled to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yulin were then banished to Yili.

sentences.zh: 明年，召還。

translations.literal: The next year they were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they were recalled.

sentences.zh: 授刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Shifen was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十二年六月，特擢江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifty-second year he was specially promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifty-second year he was specially promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，高郵州吏以偽印徵賦，事發，巡撫閔鶚元以下皆坐重譴。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year a clerk of Gaoyou prefecture collected taxes with a forged seal; when the affair broke, Governor Min Eyuan and those below him all received heavy censure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year a Gaoyou clerk collected taxes with a forged seal; when the scandal broke, Governor Min Eyuan and his subordinates all received severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 上以按察使得奏事，士棻見巡撫以下互相徇隱，置若罔聞，士棻本起廢籍，尤負恩，命奪職；

translations.literal: Because the provincial judicial commissioner could memorialize directly, the emperor held that Shifen had seen the governor and those below mutually concealing wrongdoing yet acting as if he heard nothing; Shifen had originally risen from disgrace and owed special gratitude—he was ordered stripped of office;
translations.idiomatic: Because a provincial judicial commissioner could memorialize directly to the throne, the emperor held that Shifen had watched the governor and his subordinates cover for one another yet acted as if he noticed nothing; Shifen had been raised from disgrace and owed special gratitude—he was stripped of office;

sentences.zh: 總督書麟等請遣戍，上許納贖。

translations.literal: Governor-General Shu Lin and others requested exile; the emperor permitted redemption instead.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shu Lin and others asked that he be banished, but the emperor allowed him to redeem the sentence instead.

sentences.zh: 尋复授刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he requested leave to return home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he asked to retire home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 士棻治獄，虛公周密，每有所平反。

translations.literal: Shifen heard cases with open fairness and thorough care, and often obtained reversals of wrongful judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen judged cases with open fairness and meticulous care, and often reversed wrongful verdicts.

sentences.zh: 章丘民辛存義索逋於屠者，死於途，旁置屠刀。

translations.literal: A townsman of Zhangqiu, Xin Cunyi, was collecting a debt from a butcher and died on the road; a butcher's knife lay beside him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangqiu a man named Xin Cunyi went to collect a debt from a butcher and died on the road with a butcher's knife lying beside him.

sentences.zh: 縣吏坐屠殺人。

translations.literal: County clerks convicted the butcher of murder.
translations.idiomatic: The county officials convicted the butcher of murder.

sentences.zh: 士棻奉命詣讞，躬訪於村女，別得罪人，屠乃雪。

translations.literal: Shifen was ordered to judge the case; he personally inquired of a village woman, identified the real culprit, and the butcher was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen was ordered to hear the case; he questioned a village woman in person, found the real culprit, and cleared the butcher.

sentences.zh: 旗丁有兄弟異母而同居者，兄鰥，弟有婦，夜為人戕，母訴長子姦殺。

translations.literal: Among banner bondservants were half-brothers living together: the elder was a widower, the younger had a wife; one night someone was killed; the mother accused the elder son of adultery and murder.
translations.idiomatic: Among banner bondservants were half-brothers living together—the elder a widower, the younger with a wife; one night the younger's wife was killed, and the mother accused the elder son of adultery and murder.

sentences.zh: 士棻蒞視，長子伏地哭，無一語。

translations.literal: When Shifen came to inspect, the elder son lay prostrate weeping and said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: When Shifen arrived to inspect the case, the elder son lay face down weeping and would not speak.

sentences.zh: 在側指畫者，母之侄也。

translations.literal: The one at his side gesturing and directing was the mother's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: The man at his side gesturing and prompting him was the mother's nephew.

sentences.zh: 士棻審視良久，叱其侄曰：「殺人者汝也！」

translations.literal: Shifen studied the scene long, then shouted at the nephew: "You are the killer!"
translations.idiomatic: Shifen studied the scene a long while, then shouted at the nephew: "You are the killer!"

sentences.zh: 侄股栗具伏。

translations.literal: The nephew's legs trembled and he fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew's legs gave way and he confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 泰安嫠顏氏富而子幼，夫弟強之嫁，走訴部。

translations.literal: In Tai'an the widow Yan was wealthy and her son young; her husband's younger brother forced her to remarry; she fled to petition the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an the widow Yan was wealthy and her son still young; her husband's younger brother tried to force her to remarry, and she fled to petition the ministry.

sentences.zh: 或餽士棻白金五千，士棻拒之，卒論如律。

translations.literal: Someone offered Shifen five thousand taels of silver; he refused, and in the end judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Someone offered Shifen five thousand taels of silver; he refused it and in the end ruled according to law.

sentences.zh: 邳州民有舅訟甥者，謂其發母墓，罪殊死。

translations.literal: In Pizhou an uncle sued his nephew, alleging he had opened his mother's grave—a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: In Pizhou an uncle sued his nephew, claiming he had opened his mother's grave—a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 士棻疑之，為覆讞。

translations.literal: Shifen was suspicious and re-judged the case.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen was suspicious and reopened the case.

sentences.zh: 蓋甥為前母子，舅則後母兄。

translations.literal: It turned out the nephew was son of the first wife; the uncle was elder brother of the stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: It turned out the nephew was the son of a former wife, while the uncle was the elder brother of the stepmother.

sentences.zh: 後母憎長子，舅誑之曰：「汝母墓有蛇跡。」

translations.literal: The stepmother hated the elder son; the uncle deceived him, saying: "There are snake tracks at your mother's grave."
translations.idiomatic: The stepmother hated the elder son; the uncle deceived him, saying: "There are snake tracks at your mother's grave."

sentences.zh: 甥與其妻往視，舅伺叢墓間，執詣縣。

translations.literal: The nephew and his wife went to look; the uncle waited among the graves, seized them, and handed them over to the county.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew and his wife went to look; the uncle lay in wait among the graves, seized them, and handed them over to the county.

sentences.zh: 士棻得其情，白長子枉。

translations.literal: Shifen got to the truth and declared the elder son had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen learned the truth and declared the elder son had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 士棻嘗曰：「刑官之弊，莫大於成見。

translations.literal: Shifen once said: "Among the failings of penal officials, none is greater than fixed preconceptions.
translations.idiomatic: Shifen once said: "Among the failings of penal officials, none is greater than fixed preconceptions.

sentences.zh: 聽訟有成見，強人從我，不能盡其情，是客氣也。

translations.literal: If one hears cases with a fixed view, forcing others to agree and unable to exhaust the facts—that is borrowed arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: If one hears cases with a fixed view, forcing others to one's own opinion and failing to exhaust the facts—that is borrowed arrogance.

sentences.zh: 斷罪有成見，或偏於嚴明，因求能折獄名；

translations.literal: If one passes judgment with a fixed view, leaning toward severity and sharpness to win a name for decisive adjudication;
translations.idiomatic: If one passes judgment with a fixed view, leaning toward severity and sharpness to win a name for breaking difficult cases;

sentences.zh: 或偏於寬厚，自以為陰德：皆私心也。」

translations.literal: or leaning toward leniency and thinking oneself virtuous in secret—all of this is private interest."
translations.idiomatic: or leaning toward leniency and calling it hidden virtue—all of that is private interest."

sentences.zh: 高宗知其才，屢坐譴，終不使廢棄，仍俾為刑官。

translations.literal: The Gaozong knew his talent; though repeatedly faulted and censured, he was never cast aside and was still employed as a criminal judge.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong recognized his ability; though he was rebuked and punished again and again, he was never discarded, and was still kept in the office of criminal judge.

sentences.zh: 世傳其再起復欲用為侍郎，和珅實尼之雲。

translations.literal: It was rumored in the world that when he rose again they wished to appoint him vice minister, but Heshen in fact obstructed it, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that when he returned to office there was again talk of making him vice minister—but Heshen, it was said, blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: =金簡=金簡，賜姓金佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人，初隸內務府漢軍。

translations.literal: Jin Jian. Jin Jian, granted the surname Jinjia, was of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner, originally registered with the Han Army of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Jian, granted the surname Jinjia, belonged to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and was originally attached to the Han Army of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 父三保，武備院卿。

translations.literal: His father Sanbao was Director of the Armory Department.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sanbao served as Director of the Armory Department.

sentences.zh: 金簡，乾隆中授內務府筆帖式，累遷奉宸院卿。

translations.literal: Jin Jian, during Qianlong, was appointed a clerk of the Imperial Household Department and was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Hunting Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, Jin Jian entered the Imperial Household Department as a clerk and rose in turn to Director of the Imperial Hunting Lodge.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，授總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was appointed Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was made Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 監武英殿刻書，充四庫全書副總裁，專司考覈督催。

translations.literal: He supervised printing at the Hall of Military Glory, served as associate chief compiler of the Complete Library in Four Sections, and was specially charged with examination and urging completion.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw printing at the Hall of Military Glory, served as associate chief compiler of the Complete Library in Four Sections, and was charged specifically with review and expediting the work.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授戶部侍郎，管錢法堂，鑲黃旗漢軍副都統，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, placed in charge of the Bureau of Currency, made Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner, and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he became Vice Minister of Revenue, overseeing the Bureau of Currency, was appointed Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner, and received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十年，奏：「京局鼓鑄，每年七十五卯，錢九十二萬七千三百五十千。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized: "The capital mints cast coin in seventy-five cycles each year, producing nine hundred twenty-seven thousand three hundred fifty strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he submitted a memorial: "The capital mints strike coin in seventy-five casting cycles annually, turning out nine hundred twenty-seven thousand three hundred fifty strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 歲馀二萬馀千，加以節年馀存，遇閏侭可抵放。

translations.literal: Each year there remains a surplus of more than twenty thousand strings; together with surplus accumulated over successive years, in an intercalary year it can fully cover disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand strings remain each year; with the surplus stored up over the years, even in an intercalary year disbursement can be fully covered.

sentences.zh: 請裁去閏月四卯。」

translations.literal: I request eliminating the four casting cycles in intercalary months."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the four intercalary-month casting cycles be abolished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，命纂四庫薈要，署工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was ordered to compile the Essentials of the Four Treasuries and was appointed acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was charged with compiling the Essentials of the Four Treasuries and appointed acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 命赴盛京察平允庫項虧短，關防拉薩禮等治罪如律。

translations.literal: He was ordered to proceed to Mukden to investigate shortfalls in the treasury accounts, and Guanfang, Lasali, and others were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Mukden to investigate missing funds in the treasury, and Guanfang, Lasali, and others were punished as the law required.

sentences.zh: 奏定盛京銀庫章程，下部議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized establishing regulations for the Mukden silver treasury, which the ministry deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted regulations for the Mukden silver treasury; the ministry approved them and they were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，命總理工部。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was ordered to take charge of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was placed in charge of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，擢工部尚書、鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Works and Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he rose to Minister of Works and Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，請疏濬盧溝橋中泓五孔水道，並請定三、四年疏濬一次。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he requested dredging the five central sluices of the Lu Gou Bridge channel, and requested fixing dredging once every three or four years.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year he asked that the five central channels beneath Lu Gou Bridge be dredged, and that dredging be scheduled once every three or four years.

sentences.zh: 五十年，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he took part in the banquet honoring a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 四庫全書成，議敘。

translations.literal: When the Complete Library in Four Sections was completed, merits were deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Complete Library in Four Sections was finished, rewards for service were reckoned.

sentences.zh: 命修葺明陵，請加築思陵月台，並拓享殿、宮門。

translations.literal: He was ordered to repair the Ming tombs, and requested additional construction of the moon platform at Siling and expansion of the sacrificial hall and palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with restoring the Ming tombs and proposed raising the moon platform at Siling and enlarging the sacrificial hall and palace gate.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，故安南國王黎維祁聽所屬黃益曉、黎光霽等禀請歸國，命金簡察治，益曉、光霽等並發遣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, the former king of Annam, Le Duy Ky, heeding his subordinates Huang Yixiao, Le Guangji, and others who petitioned to return to their country, was ordered investigated and handled by Jin Jian; Yixiao, Guangji, and the others were all deported.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year Le Duy Ky, the former king of Annam, gave ear to Huang Yixiao, Le Guangji, and others under him who petitioned to return home; Jin Jian was ordered to investigate and settle the matter, and Yixiao, Guangji, and the rest were all sent away.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel as minister.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，卒，令皇孫綿懃奠醊，賜祭葬，諡勤恪。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he died; the emperor ordered the imperial grandson Mianqin to pour libations, granted ceremonial burial, and posthumously titled him Qinke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-ninth year; the emperor had his grandson Mianqin offer libations, granted a state funeral, and gave him the posthumous name Qinke.

sentences.zh: 金簡女弟為高宗貴妃。

translations.literal: Jin Jian's younger sister by a different mother was an imperial consort of the Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Jian's half-sister was an imperial consort of the Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，仁宗命其族改入滿洲，賜姓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, the Renzong ordered his clan transferred into the Manchu register and granted the surname.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiaqing the Renzong had his family entered into the Manchu rolls and granted them the surname.

sentences.zh: 缊布，金簡子。

translations.literal: Yun Bu was Jin Jian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Bu was the son of Jin Jian.

sentences.zh: 初授拜唐阿，擢藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: At first appointed a baitangga, he was promoted to guard with blue plume.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a baitangga and was raised to imperial guard with a blue plume.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十八年，授泰宁鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was appointed regional commander of Taiping Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 48 he was made regional commander at Taiping Garrison.

sentences.zh: 六十年，召授總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was summoned and appointed Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was recalled and appointed Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，授鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he was appointed Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 3 he became Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 四年，授工部侍郎，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Vice Minister of Works and awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 奏請增設內務府養育兵，上斥其例外乞恩，意在沽名。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting additional sustenance soldiers for the Imperial Household Department; the emperor reprimanded him for seeking favor outside precedent, intending to win a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to add sustenance soldiers to the Imperial Household Department; the emperor rebuked him for begging favor outside established practice—an attempt, he said, to buy a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 俄以清字摺誤書孝聖憲皇后徽號，奪官，予四品頂帶，留佐領。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, in a Manchu memorial he mistakenly wrote the honorific title of Empress Xiaoshengxian; his office was stripped, he was given a fourth-rank insignia, and retained as company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a Manchu memorial of his misspelled the honorific of Empress Xiaoshengxian; he was removed from office, given a fourth-rank cap button, and kept on as company commander.

sentences.zh: 旋复授正紅旗蒙古副都統、總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was again appointed Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Mongol Plain Red Banner and Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Deputy Lieutenant-General of the Mongol Plain Red Banner and Grand Minister Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 五年，授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢工部尚書、鑲紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Minister of Works and Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he rose to Minister of Works and Lieutenant-General of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 九年，署戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he acted as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：曰修奉使治水，利澤施於生民；

translations.literal: Commentary. The commentary says: Yuexiu on mission managed water control, and benefit spread to the living people;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Qiu Yuexiu, sent on missions to manage waterworks, brought lasting benefit to the people;

sentences.zh: 紹詩疏律義，尚平恕：皆有子克承厥緒。

translations.literal: Shaoshi expounded the meaning of law and valued leniency and forbearance: each had sons able to carry on their line.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoshi clarified the principles of law and held to clemency: in each case a son proved able to continue the work;

sentences.zh: 循琦、際華、秀先迴翔台省，以篤謹被主知；

translations.literal: Xunqi, Jihua, and Xiuxian moved between the censorate and ministries, known to their ruler for steadfast care;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xunqi, Wang Jihua, and Cao Xiuxian shifted between the censorate and the ministries, winning their sovereign's trust through steady diligence;

sentences.zh: 文埴眷尤厚，不阿時相，潔其身以去：皆彬彬平世令僕才也。

translations.literal: Wenzhi enjoyed especially thick favor, would not flatter the chief minister of the time, and kept himself clean in departing: all were cultured talents fit for service as excellent ministers in a tranquil age.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi received especially warm favor, refused to curry favor with the chief minister of the day, and withdrew with his integrity intact: each was a polished talent suited to peaceful times and worthy service.

sentences.zh: 乾隆之季，民窮盜起，煌父子言鄉里民間疾苦，高宗不以為忤。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianlong the people were impoverished and bandits arose; Huang and his son spoke of the hardships of folk in their districts, and the Gaozong did not take it amiss.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Qianlong, as the people grew poor and banditry spread, Zhou Huang and his son spoke plainly of local suffering, and the Gaozong did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 金簡起戚畹，所論鑄錢、葺明陵，及黎維祁乞歸國，並關國故，故比而次之。

translations.literal: Jin Jian rose from imperial affines; his discussions of coin casting, repair of the Ming tombs, and Le Duy Ky's petition to return home all touched former national affairs, and so he is ranked here in comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Jian came up through imperial marriage ties; his proposals on coinage, restoration of the Ming tombs, and Le Duy Ky's plea to return—all touched matters of national consequence—and so he is placed here in due order among them.
